answer: Timed arrival-gap kernel. Each identity must submit its first message inside a per-epoch arrival window whose width is derived from a shared crystal clock and a random seed; the kernel rejects any burst exceeding one registration per window slot. Enforcement is local: surplus identities collide and are dropped. The attacker pays in wall-clock scheduling—to pass, each identity needs a distinct slot, so N identities cost N sequential windows (e.g., 12s each), and forged timestamps fail against the clock relic held by validators.
